title: How to Beat Surveillance Pricing Before It Bleeds You Dry
gist: Groundwork Collaborative CEO Lindsay Owens argues software and AI have ended the 150-year fixed-price norm, enabling surveillance (personalized) pricing via loyalty data and agentic commerce (Walmart's Sparky carts run 35% higher), and calls for fiduciary duties for shopping agents as state laws spread in Connecticut, New Jersey and Maryland.

insights.claim: Lindsay Owens argues the fixed price, a 150-year norm since John Wanamaker's price tags, is under attack if not gone, and new technology is the biggest contributor to its end.
insights.speaker: Reece Rogers
insights.so_what: Dynamic and personalized pricing shifts consumer surplus to sellers and draws regulatory risk.
insights.locator: It is under attack, if not gone

insights.claim: Surveillance pricing is first-degree price discrimination, using personal data to estimate an individual's willingness to pay, which can exploit urgency rather than ability to pay.
insights.speaker: Reece Rogers
insights.so_what: Firms with rich first-party data can extract more margin, but face mounting backlash.
insights.quote: willingness to pay isn't the same thing as ability to pay
insights.locator: Could you explain what you mean

insights.claim: Loyalty programs are sophisticated data harvesting that, Owens says, no longer hold up their end of the bargain on discounts, echoing Duke economist Curtis Taylor's 2004 warning that firms would charge their most eager customers more.
insights.speaker: Reece Rogers
insights.so_what: Loyalty data monetization is a margin lever for retailers and a target for regulators.
insights.quote: Loyalty programs are sophisticated data harvesting.

insights.claim: A McDonald's app data request produced a 515-page dossier estimating a zero percent chance the user would ever stop being a customer.
insights.speaker: Reece Rogers
insights.so_what: Illustrates the granularity of consumer data held by large consumer brands.

insights.claim: Walmart says Sparky cart totals are 35 percent higher than non-Sparky cart totals, which Owens cites as an early warning that agentic commerce supercharges upselling.
insights.speaker: Reece Rogers
insights.so_what: AI shopping assistants can lift basket size materially, a revenue tailwind for retailers deploying them.
insights.quote: Walmart says Sparky cart totals are 35 percent higher than non-Sparky cart totals.

insights.claim: Owens says agentic commerce is at an inflection point and should be regulated so agents must act in consumers' interests, like the best-interest or fiduciary standards of realtors and lawyers.
insights.speaker: Reece Rogers
insights.so_what: Fiduciary rules for AI agents would constrain monetization models for agentic commerce.

insights.claim: Groundwork Collaborative exposed Instacart's experiment treating millions of Americans as guinea pigs in pricing A/B tests without their knowledge.
insights.speaker: Reece Rogers
insights.so_what: Undisclosed price experiments create reputational and regulatory risk for platforms like Instacart.
insights.locator: The second thing is they figure out

insights.claim: Dozens of bills targeting surveillance and algorithmic pricing were introduced this year, with some signed into law in Connecticut, New Jersey and Maryland, while federal action moves more slowly.
insights.speaker: Reece Rogers
insights.so_what: A growing state patchwork raises compliance costs for algorithmic pricing.

insights.claim: Owens sees surveillance pricing as a nonpartisan issue, having worked for Senator Elizabeth Warren and testified on behalf of Senator Josh Hawley.
insights.speaker: Reece Rogers
insights.so_what: Bipartisan concern raises the odds of eventual federal action.
insights.quote: I think this issue is a nonpartisan one.

insights.claim: Consumers can counter personalized pricing by comparing within brands across logged-in vs logged-out, app vs web vs store, VPN geographies, and with friends, though at a high cost in time.
insights.speaker: Reece Rogers
insights.so_what: Consumer workarounds limit but do not eliminate personalized-pricing gains.
